label: First input token from a fixed token set (t=0), plus first copy step of short sequences
explanation: Two contexts. (1) Step 0 (about 74% of activation mass): fires on every sequence whose first token is in {a,c,e,f,g,h,i,j,l,m,n,o,r,x,y,z,0}, with precision 1.0 per token, and never when the first token is in {b,d,k,p,q,s,t,u,v,w,1,2,3}. Magnitude at t=0 depends only on the token: r, o, e, 0 and x are strongest (about 0.16-0.21 of max), and i, m, h are weakest (about 0.01-0.02). (2) The step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, where the first original token is fed back in and the second is being output), about 26% of mass. It holds almost all of the largest activations (up to max), mostly when L=3 (precision about 0.91). It is weaker and less reliable at L=4 (precision about 0.34, about 13% of mass) and nearly absent for L>=5. At L=3 it fires even for first tokens outside the step-0 set (e.g. t). The step-0 token set does not cleanly decide when it fires at L=4. Essentially silent at all other original-phase steps (rare weak firing at t=1), at <DEL>, and at later copy steps. Dev: P 0.996, R 0.913, F1 0.953, mass recall 0.867. Adding L=4 to the copy clause raises mass recall to 0.995 but drops F1 to 0.925.

issues: All the factual claims check out on the dev split. At t=0 with the 17-token set: precision 1.0 and 100% of t=0 activity (56640/56640), about 74% of activation mass. Every other t=0 token is silent. L=3 recall_idx=1: precision about 0.91 (0.94 when the first token is in the set, 0.87 when it is not). L=4 recall_idx=1: precision 0.34, 12.7% of mass. recall_idx=1 at L>=5: precision 0.004. t=1: 0.3% of steps, negligible. Zero activity at <DEL> and at recall_idx>=2. Test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.996, R 0.914, F1 0.953, mass recall 0.868).

One systematic miss class remains: L=4, recall_idx=1. Test misses are dominated by step-5 examples from this context, and it holds about 13% of activation mass, about the same as the L=3 clause. The explanation mentions it but leaves it out of the predicate.

The explanation's claim that the step-0 token set does not cleanly decide L=4 firing is only half right. Firing at L=4 is graded by the first token. Tokens c, e, f, o, r, x fire 62-82% of the time, while k, w, 2 and similar tokens fire about 4%. Firing also rises when the later original tokens fall outside the step-0 set: with orig(1..3) all outside it, precision is 0.94. So there is clear structure here that the label leaves out.

Adding the high-precision L=4 subset improves the predicate. Test F1 goes from 0.953 to 0.964 and mass recall from 0.868 to 0.937, at a precision cost of 0.996 to 0.983. The improvement is modest but systematic.
skeptic.revised_label: First input token from a fixed token set (t=0); also the step after <DEL> in short sequences: always at L=3, and at L=4 when the first token is c/e/f/o/r/x
